title: Canary analyzer: fetch error budget status + emit budget risk signals
author: Devon Price
release_notes: Analyzer now pulls tier-aware error budget status and annotates canary runs with a budget risk state (OK/AT_RISK/EXHAUSTED). This is used by rollout tooling to gate progression and by SRE to correlate regressions with budget burn.
body:
## Summary
This change extends the perf-canary analyzer to consume the new error budget status API and tag every canary result with a normalized `budget_risk` signal. The intent is to make error budget burn a first-class input into canary analysis (warn now; block later), and to reduce time-to-diagnosis when we see quality/latency regressions correlate with budget spikes.

Key outcomes:
- Adds a `BudgetStatusClient` that fetches current budget status scoped by `{tier, service, region}` (and optionally `{route, model}` when present in the canary config).
- Annotates analyzer output with `budget_risk_state` and a small set of budget fields (remaining %, burn rates, window) for downstream gating + UI.
- Emits a lightweight metric + structured log with the budget risk state to support dashboard overlays.

## Background / Motivation
As part of the tiered SLO + error budget enforcement initiative, rollouts should “feel” budget burn before we ship changes broadly. Today the analyzer only checks performance regressions (TTFT/p95/p99) and correctness checks; it does not consider whether the service is currently at risk of exhausting the budget. This PR wires in budget status so we can:
1) Flag canary runs as risky when budgets are already burning, and
2) Avoid promoting rollouts when the system is already unstable.

Related:
- Linear: ENG-2427, ENG-2422, ENG-2421
- Control plane budget-check endpoint: redwood#18421
- SLI attribution follow-up from SUP-3972

## Implementation details
### 1) Budget status fetch
- New config block under `analyzer`:
  - `error_budget.enabled` (default false)
  - `error_budget.endpoint` (e.g. `https://control-plane.prod.redwood.internal`)
  - `error_budget.timeout_ms` (default 750ms)
  - `error_budget.fail_open` (default true)
  - `error_budget.cache_ttl_seconds` (default 30)
- Fetch occurs once per canary run and is cached by `{tier, service, region, route, model}` key.
- Uses service-to-service auth via the existing `CANARY_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN` env var (same wiring as the existing rollout metadata fetch).

### 2) Normalized risk mapping
The control plane returns a more detailed budget payload than we want to leak into every canary artifact. We normalize to:
- `budget_risk_state`: `OK | AT_RISK | EXHAUSTED | UNKNOWN`
- `budget_remaining_percent`: stringified float with 2 decimals
- `budget_burn_rate_1h` and `budget_burn_rate_6h` (if present)
- `budget_window`: `"28d"` today (carried through for future window flexibility)

Mapping logic:
- `EXHAUSTED` if remaining <= 0 OR policy state indicates exhaustion.
- `AT_RISK` if remaining <= 10% OR burn rate thresholds exceed policy.
- `UNKNOWN` if request fails or payload missing required fields.
- If `fail_open=true` and fetch fails, we still run analysis and set `UNKNOWN`.

### 3) Analyzer output changes
- Adds a new top-level result annotation line in the summary:
  - `Budget risk: AT_RISK (remaining 7.42%, burn1h 3.6x, burn6h 1.4x)`
- Adds JSON fields to the emitted artifact for CI ingestion.
- Adds metrics:
  - `perf_canary_budget_risk_state_total{state=...,tier=...,service=...,region=...}`

## Screenshots / sample output
Example analyzer summary snippet:
"Canary: gateway-chat-streaming/us-east-1 (tier=hosted)
Performance: PASS
Correctness: PASS
Budget risk: AT_RISK (remaining 7.42%, burn1h 3.6x, burn6h 1.4x)"

## Testing
- Unit tests for normalization and caching behavior.
- Integration test uses a stubbed control plane server with 200/500/timeout cases.
- Verified locally with `./bin/analyze --config configs/gateway_chat_streaming.yaml` against staging control plane.

## Rollout plan
1) Land behind `error_budget.enabled=false` by default.
2) Enable for the pilot set of services (gateway + routing) in staging first.
3) Enable in prod in warn-only mode (rollout UI displays the risk state but does not block).
4) Follow-up: wire into rollout gating once policy is in soft-block mode (tracked in ENG-2427).

## Notes / follow-ups
- This does not implement blocking behavior; it only annotates results. The gate lives in the rollout controller.
- Dedicated tier behavior: we scope by `{tier=dedicated, service, region, pool_id?}`; pool-level mapping is not available yet from the control plane API, so this PR only passes through `customer_id`/`pool_id` if present in config and ignored otherwise.
- If this increases control plane QPS materially, we can bump TTL and/or batch requests; current TTL=30s + per-run fetch should be fine.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration test added
- [x] Backward compatible (feature disabled by default)
- [x] Updated sample configs + docs
commits: analyzer: add BudgetStatusClient with caching + timeouts
analyzer: normalize budget payload into BudgetRisk annotation
configs: add error_budget block to sample configs (disabled by default)
tests: add unit + integration tests for budget fetch + normalization
metrics: emit budget risk state counter + structured log fields
review_conversation: Aisha Bello: Can we make sure this is fail-open? I don't want budget endpoint flakiness to block perf regression detection.
Devon Price (author): Yep—default is `fail_open=true` and we set `budget_risk_state=UNKNOWN` on error. Only annotation changes; analysis continues.
Benji Okafor: What auth does this use? Please avoid introducing a second token path; we already have CANARY_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN in CI.
Devon Price (author): Reused CANARY_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN and the existing request wrapper. Added explicit redaction in logs; token never printed.
Sergio Costa: Can you add caching? Without it, canary fanout will hammer control plane during incident drills.
Devon Price (author): Added 30s TTL cache keyed by {tier,service,region,route,model}. Also added a hard timeout (750ms default).
Jordan Lee: The risk mapping should match policy semantics. Remaining<=10% isn't always 'at risk' if burn is low; do we have burn rates?
Devon Price (author): We map AT_RISK if remaining<=10% OR burn rates exceed threshold. If burn rates missing, we only use remaining. Added tests for both cases.
Aisha Bello: Please include tier in the emitted metric labels but be careful with route/model cardinality.
Devon Price (author): Metrics are only {state,tier,service,region}. Route/model are only in artifact annotations (not metrics).
Sergio Costa: Docs update looks good. One request: add a note about `UNKNOWN` meaning fail-open and link to ENG-2427.
post_merge_notes: Enabled in staging for gateway-chat-streaming canary (warn-only) and confirmed annotations appear in artifacts. Next: have rollout controller consume `budget_risk_state` for soft-block (ENG-2427).
